title: Hello World Infer 30s runbook + pricing experiments
body:
Goal summary

Write a compact, testable developer quickstart and a set of pricing-language experiments that highlight Redwood Inference's hosted API as the lowest-friction path from prototype -> production for engineers. The deliverable is a 30-second "hello" flow, a 3-step guided code sample for a 2-minute demo, and 4 pricing copy variants to A/B test on signup and pricing pages.

Audience and primary persona

- Primary: Backend/Full‑stack engineers who want to ship an LLM feature without managing GPUs. Care about latency, predictable costs, and easy rollbacks.
- Secondary: ML engineers who own model quality and want performance transparency when moving from notebook to endpoint.

Core developer-first value frames (short)

1) Immediate feedback loop: "Get a model running in 30 seconds" — short friction metric focused on time-to-first-token.
2) Predictable economics: "Per-call unit pricing, transparent latency anchors" — emphasize token + invocation clarity, example math.
3) No ops lock-in: "Start hosted, move to Dedicated or Private with the same API" — highlight identical API surface.
4) Production primitives: "Built-in fallbacks, per-route SLOs, and observability" — call out debugging hooks and tracing.

Quickstart and UX flows

A. "30s hello" (microflow for landing page)
- Headline: "Hello in 30s: Your LLM endpoint, no infra"
- One-liner: "Create an API key, paste this 3-line cURL, get text back"
- Flow: sign up -> create API key -> run cURL example -> view streaming output in terminal
- Success metric: developer sees a token returned within 30s after signup completion.

B. "2-minute integrate" (code-first onboarding)
- Step 0: scaffolding repo link + single-file example (node/python).
- Step 1: set env var REDWOOD_API_KEY and run `npm start` or `python3 hello_infer.py`.
- Step 2: swap prompt and call model with a single POST, see streaming output.
- Step 3: add a single route in your app that proxies with request-level tags for latency billing.
- Success metric: integration -> deployable stub in < 2 minutes; track time to first successful CI-run.

C. Local dev experience / mock server
- Ship a tiny local binary (redwood-mock) that returns canned responses matching the hosted API shape so engineers can develop offline against the same SDK surface.
- Messaging point: "Develop locally, test in CI, flip the key to call hosted."

Pricing language experiments (4 variants)

Objective: find copy that reduces signup friction while setting correct cost expectations for latency-sensitive workloads. Each variant tested on pricing page and within quickstart microcopy.

Variant A — Unit clarity (baseline)
- "Pay per token for generation, per-call for embeddings. No surprise fees."
- Example snippet: "~$0.0006 per generated token. 10K tokens typical for a quick prototype: ~$6."

Variant B — Predictable buckets (anchor)
- "Choose a bucket: Starter (metred), Committed (discounted burst), Enterprise (SLA)."
- Microcopy: "Starter covers casual dev use; committed plans reserve throughput and lower unit cost."

Variant C — Time-to-value first
- "Free tier + 30s demo credit: spin up, get results, then see exact per-call cost."
- Microcopy: "We give you credits that are consumed only when you complete the first successful API response — no credit used for signup churn."

Variant D — Outcome pricing language (experiment)
- "Anchor to developer outcomes: $X per 1000 inference calls under 2s latency"
- Microcopy: "If you need predictable sub-2s throughput, choose a performance plan with SLAs and committed bursts."

Competitive differentiation notes (concise)

Comp set: major LLM APIs (provider-as-a-service), cloud-managed endpoints, self-hosted runtimes (open-source + infra).

- Against cloud providers: highlight lower coordination overhead (no infra provisioning), transparent per-route latency and token accounting, and dev ergonomics vs. long-managed service setup.
- Against LLM API providers: avoid competing on highest model quality claim; instead emphasize predictable serving characteristics (latency SLOs, fallback routing), identical API across hosted/dedicated/private, and on-ramp velocity.
- Against self-hosted infra: stress time and team cost to maintain kernels, batching, and cache correctness; Redwood's value is "production inference primitives" and fewer engineering cycles.

Sample homepage copy blocks (unique phrasing)

Hero line: "Build with LLMs, not GPUs: a hosted inference API engineers actually want to use."
Subhead: "From prototype to SLA-backed deploys — same API, faster time-to-value, clearer unit economics."
CTA variants: "Run your first request — 30s" / "Try a 2-minute demo app" / "Compare costs on your workload"

Pricing microcopy (examples to A/B)

- One-line anchor: "Charged by usage: tokens + optional throughput reservation."
- Example billing snippet: "A chat message (~150 tokens) ≈ $0.09 at starter unit rates; reserved capacity lowers that to $0.04."
- FAQ blurb: "We bill tokens generated and consumed; cached responses are credited back when cache hits occur."

Launch experiments and metrics to measure

1) Quickstart conversion funnel: landing -> API key created -> request made -> secret exchanged -> first successful token. Target 40% of signups hit the first token within 10 minutes.
2) Pricing copy lift: run four-way A/B on signup-to-commit conversion and average first-week spend. Look for highest conversion with acceptable LTV.
3) Time-to-first-meaningful-call: instrument SDK and sample apps to measure durations. Target median < 45s.
4) Support contact rate: measure how many trial users email/raise tickets in first 24h; lower is better.

Open questions / risks

- Credit consumption model: can we guarantee the “demo credit only consumed after first successful response” behavior with current billing plumbing? Ops alignment needed.
- Local mock parity: shipping a reliable mock that matches API nuance (streaming, chunking) is non-trivial but high ROI. Engineering estimate required.
- Pricing message legal: when anchoring to latency (sub-2s), we must avoid committing to guarantees without appropriate SLA/plan gating. Legal review needed.

Next steps (action items)

- Align with infra and billing on demo credit gating (Owners: Ethan, Priya) — due 2025-10-09.
- Prototype the 2-minute sample app in Node and Python; add to samples repo and CI (Owner: Lia) — due 2025-09-20.
- Create landing AB test variants for the four pricing microcopy experiments (Owner: GTM front end) — due 2025-10-01.
- Draft support doc for local mock usage and developer workflow (Owner: Developer Experience) — due 2025-09-25.

Appendix: short script for a 30s demo (copy to landing CTA)

1) Sign up and copy API key
2) Run in terminal:
   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n     -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n     -d '{"model":"redwood-compact-1","input":"Say hello from Redwood in one sentence."}'

3) Watch streaming text appear — change the input and run again.

Notes to reviewer

- This is intentionally compact and experiment-focused. I want feedback on the pricing anchors and whether a latency-anchored plan is acceptable to product/legal. Also check the signup flow metrics; instrumentation will be needed in the onboarding service.

Keywords: 30s, hello, quickstart, demo credits, token math, developer-first
